//: Copy to config.json and fill in (or use the dashboard's Settings page). An environment variable overrides each value here, from .env or the shell; its name leads each `// <key>` note (e.g. BFMR_MIN_INSURANCE_VALUE=999 python -m sync_tracking). docs/configuration.md lists them all. Booleans are true/false; anything unrecognised is false, so a money switch fails closed on a typo.
//2: EVERY setting lives here, including the container schedule. .env is only the override layer, for dev or host-specific values (a temporary LOOKBACK_DAYS, a host's own RUN_INTERVAL_HOURS).

browser_use.// api_key: BROWSER_USE_API_KEY — required. The cloud browser the scrapers, receipt capture and the Costco token grab run in.

alerts.//: Configure at least one channel. With neither, an unattended host reports a logged-out session or a failed run to nobody. Test with `python -m alerts.notifier`.
alerts.// discord_enabled: DISCORD_ALERTS_ENABLED — post alerts to the Discord webhook below. Off keeps the URL and sends nothing there.
alerts.// gmail_enabled: GMAIL_ALERTS_ENABLED — email alerts from the Gmail account below. Off keeps the account and sends nothing.
alerts.// gmail_app_password: GMAIL_APP_PASSWORD — a Google APP PASSWORD, not your account password. This account is only for alerts: the BFMR auto-reply's mailbox is entered separately under buying_groups.bfmr, even when it is the same account.
alerts.// cap_warn_percent: CASHBACK_CAP_WARN_PERCENT — alert (and a card on the overview) once this percent of a card's spend limit is spent in the period; 0 = off.
alerts.// cap_warn_dollars: CASHBACK_CAP_WARN_DOLLARS — alert once this little of a card's spend limit is left in the period; 0 = off. Either threshold triggers.

scraping.// lookback_days: LOOKBACK_DAYS — CALENDAR days back, counting today as 0. 1 = today and yesterday.
scraping.// default_cashback_rate: DEFAULT_CASHBACK_RATE — for a card not listed in `cards`. Write 2% as 0.02 or "2%", never 2.
scraping.// amazon_promo_cashback_enabled: AMAZON_PROMO_CASHBACK_ENABLED — add Amazon's per-order 'Earn N% back' promo on top of the card's rate.
scraping.// amazon_gift_card_netting_enabled: AMAZON_GIFT_CARD_NETTING_ENABLED — record the gift card (Gift Card column, subtracted in COGS) and Amazon rewards (Rewards Used column, out of the cashback basis) an order was part-paid with, so no cashback is booked on money the card never spent. false leaves them blank and COGS uses the full cost.

buying_groups.// sync_enabled: BUYING_GROUP_SYNC_ENABLED — SPENDS REAL MONEY. On, every scheduled run submits tracking numbers and files BFMR insurance unattended. Leave off until a dry run and a one-package live test have both been done. `python -m sync_tracking` ignores this.

bfmr.//: BFMR authenticates with TWO HEADERS (API-KEY / API-SECRET), not a bearer token. Both from Developer Tools in your BFMR account settings.
bfmr.// enabled: BFMR_ENABLED — this group's own switch under sync_enabled. Off, the sync leaves BFMR alone (nothing submitted, insured or read back) while other groups still run. `python -m sync_tracking --group BFMR` overrides it.
bfmr.// min_insurance_value: BFMR_MIN_INSURANCE_VALUE — only insure shipments worth at least this. BFMR charges ~0.45% with a $2.00 MINIMUM, so below roughly $450 the floor dominates and the effective rate passes 1%. 0 insures everything.
bfmr.// costco_tv_order_number_as_tracking: BFMR_COSTCO_TV_ORDER_NUMBER_AS_TRACKING — BFMR's rule for Costco TVs: the order number is the tracking number. On, a Costco row routed to BFMR whose item name matches the pattern below carries its order number as Tracking Number from ordered on (so the next run submits and insures it), and keeps it when Costco reports a carrier number.
bfmr.// costco_tv_item_pattern: BFMR_COSTCO_TV_ITEM_PATTERN — which Costco item names count as a TV for that rule (a regular expression, case-insensitive).
bfmr.// combined_package: The next five settings drive ONE feature: auto-answering BFMR's 'Combined Best Buy Package' emails (their request for the units' serial numbers + the receipt PDF). It reads and replies from its OWN Gmail account (combined_package_gmail_* below), never the alerts account.
bfmr.// combined_package_autoreply_enabled: BFMR_COMBINED_PACKAGE_AUTOREPLY_ENABLED — SENDS REAL MAIL to BFMR. On, every scheduled run answers their combined-package emails unattended. Leave off until a dry run and a supervised first send have both been done. `python -m respond_bfmr` ignores this.
bfmr.// combined_package_sender_domains: BFMR_COMBINED_PACKAGE_SENDER_DOMAINS — From-domains that count as BFMR when scanning the auto-reply's inbox, comma-separated.
bfmr.// combined_package_reply_cc: BFMR_COMBINED_PACKAGE_REPLY_CC — optional Cc on every reply: the address BFMR writes to, if requests are forwarded to the replying account (otherwise the reply shows only in that account's Sent Mail). Blank = none.
bfmr.// combined_package_gmail_address: BFMR_COMBINED_PACKAGE_GMAIL_ADDRESS / _APP_PASSWORD — the Gmail account the auto-reply reads BFMR's requests from and replies as (its own app password). Required when the auto-reply is on; it never uses the alerts account, so enter it here even if it is the same one.

mod.//: MaxOutDeals needs a bearer token AND an IP allowlist: add this machine under the firewall tab in your MOD profile, or every call is rejected. user_id and email go in the body of every request.
mod.// enabled: MAXOUTDEALS_ENABLED — this group's own switch under sync_enabled. Off, the sync leaves MOD alone while other groups still run. `python -m sync_tracking --group MOD` overrides it.

receipts.// capture_enabled: RECEIPT_CAPTURE_ENABLED — render each newly-seen order's receipt to PDF under `dir`, linked from Receipt Link. Costs money: capture opens a paid Browser-Use session (one per profile and retailer on a run with new orders). Off = a blank Receipt Link.
receipts.// dir: RECEIPTS_DIR — where the receipt files live, relative to the repo root (in Docker the mounted data/ volume, inside every backup). The Settings page keeps it within data/. The dashboard serves them at /receipts/.

// container: Read by docker/entrypoint.sh when the container starts. Irrelevant outside Docker.

container.// run_interval_hours: RUN_INTERVAL_HOURS — hours between scheduled runs. Each run spends one of MaxOutDeals' 10 daily received-items calls, so preflight warns when the interval implies more than that.
container.// run_on_start: RUN_ON_START — also run once the moment the container starts. Handy on first boot.
container.// preflight_strict: PREFLIGHT_STRICT — refuse to start when preflight fails, instead of alerting and running degraded. Off by default: a container that won't start also stops scraping, and a missed order costs more than a degraded run.
container.// timezone: TZ — the cron schedule follows this.

// web: The web dashboard (`python -m web` on a desktop; in Docker it runs inside the one container beside the scheduler). See docs/operations.md, 'The web dashboard'.

web.// enabled: WEB_ENABLED — in the container, start the dashboard beside the scheduler (and probe it in the healthcheck). false = a pure scheduler container, as before.
web.// ledger_source: WEB_LEDGER_SOURCE — `db` (the default) serves the ledger, the SQLite file in database.path; `snapshot` serves a data/ledger_backup_*.csv export instead (offline work; snapshot_path picks one). Anything else is refused at startup.
web.// snapshot_path: WEB_SNAPSHOT_PATH — a specific CSV for the snapshot backend. Blank = the newest data/ledger_backup_*.csv.
web.// ledger_cache_ttl_seconds: WEB_LEDGER_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS — how long the dashboard keeps a read of the ledger file before re-reading it, in seconds (reported by /health; ?refresh=1 on any page re-reads now).
web.// bind_host: WEB_BIND_HOST — loopback by default; set `password` before binding wider (0.0.0.0 behind Tailscale or on the LAN). The compose service publishes on 127.0.0.1 unless WEB_PUBLISH_HOST says otherwise.
web.// tool_session_minutes: WEB_TOOL_SESSION_MINUTES — the Tools page's profile-login browser session is closed for you (cookies saved) after this many minutes if you leave it open.
web.// heartbeat_stale_hours: WEB_HEARTBEAT_STALE_HOURS — hours without a completed run before the header's heartbeat pill turns stale (the pill's tooltip shows it). 0 = twice the run interval, the container healthcheck's own rule.
web.// public_url: WEB_PUBLIC_URL — the dashboard's address as YOU open it (e.g. http://192.0.2.10:8765 over WireGuard): alerts link a failure dossier to its Activity page through it. Blank = alerts name the path on the host only.
web.// allowed_hosts: WEB_ALLOWED_HOSTS — extra host NAMES the dashboard answers to, comma-separated (e.g. ledger.local; .example.com = any subdomain). An IP address, localhost and public_url's host always work; any other name is refused (this stops DNS rebinding). Read at dashboard start.
web.// password: WEB_PASSWORD — the dashboard's sign-in password. Blank = no sign-in at all, so set it BEFORE binding wider than loopback: reachable beyond this machine with no password, the dashboard serves only a page that sets one, using the setup token printed to its log. Changing it signs every device out. Read at dashboard start.
web.// session_hours: WEB_SESSION_HOURS — how long a sign-in lasts when Remember me is NOT ticked, in hours.
web.// remember_days: WEB_REMEMBER_DAYS — how long a sign-in lasts when Remember me IS ticked, in days (730 = 2 years).
web.// login_attempts: WEB_LOGIN_ATTEMPTS — wrong passwords in a row from one address before that address is locked out.
web.// login_lockout_minutes: WEB_LOGIN_LOCKOUT_MINUTES — how long that lock lasts, in minutes (0 = never lock). A lock is recorded as an alert on the Activity page.

// database: THE LEDGER: the SQLite file (ledger_db/) the scrapers' upsert, the sort, the buying-group sync, the BFMR auto-reply, the dashboard's editor and every script write and read. Included in `python -m scripts.backup`.

database.// path: LEDGER_DB_PATH — relative to the repo root (in Docker, the mounted data/ volume).

// backups: Scheduled backups: a zip of config.json, .state.json, .env and data/ (the ledger) into backups/, made by the container's own cron (`python -m scripts.backup --scheduled`). The Settings page's Backup & Restore panel shows the schedule and the zips; the oldest are deleted once more than `keep` exist. Read once at container start. Copy backups/ off the host too.

backups.// time: BACKUP_TIME — HH:MM, 24-hour, in the container's timezone (container.timezone).
backups.// days: BACKUP_DAYS — weekly: day names (mon,thu); monthly: days of the month, 1-28 (1,15). Ignored when daily. Blank = Sunday / the 1st.
backups.// keep: BACKUP_KEEP — how many zips to keep in backups/: after each new backup (scheduled or from the dashboard) the oldest beyond this are deleted. 0 = keep all.

// profiles: One Browser-Use browser identity per entry, each behind its own proxy. Amazon and Amazon Business MUST NOT share a profile (one identity for both links the accounts). `profile_id` is filled in by `python -m scripts.create_profile`.

profiles.label: profile-1
profiles.// auth: Unattended sign-in, keyed by retailer: username + password + a TOTP seed. TURN 2-STEP VERIFICATION ON with an authenticator app and paste its secret into `totp_secret`; the sign-in generates the code itself. A challenge with no seed fails the sign-in with an alert. Amazon, Amazon Business and Best Buy take a seed; Costco takes none.

profiles.label: profile-2
profiles.// auth costco: Costco sign-in, for minting a refresh token and capturing receipts; its order data needs no browser. Without it a lapsed browser session needs a human. NO `totp_secret`: Costco has no 2-step verification (if it ever adds one, the sign-in says so by name).
profiles.// auth amazon-business: Amazon Business sign-in. Without it a lapsed session records NOTHING until you re-run scripts/create_profile. `totp_secret` is the base32 key from Login & Security -> 2-step verification -> Authenticator App -> "Can't scan the barcode?"; enrol an app, not SMS/email, which nothing here can receive.

// warehouses: Which buying group an order belongs to, matched on its DELIVERY ADDRESS. A jig is a deliberately misspelled variant the group hands out ('THIRTEEN SAMMPLE DR1VE') so each order routes distinctly — it is a routing token, never a postal address, and nothing ever files it as one. BFMR, MOD (MaxOutDeals) and Personal are built in; `Personal` rows are dropped before the ledger is written.
// cards: Cashback per card, matched on the last 4 digits the scraper reads. `retailer_rates` overrides the card's overall rate at one retailer. Rates accept 0.02 or "2%" — never a bare 2.

cards.// profile: Scopes a card to one profile, when two accounts each have a card ending in the same 4 digits.
cards.name: Personal Amex Gold

cards.// virtual: A virtual card number: add `virtual_of` (its card's last 4) and it earns that card's rates and shares its caps. The Taxes page asks no sign-up bonus for it.
cards.name: Citi Double Cash (virtual)

cards.// caps: Spend caps on the boosted rate: past `spend_limit` of spend in the period (within the cap's retailers, or every retailer when `retailers` is empty) purchases earn `fallback_rate`; the purchase that crosses the line earns the blend. `resets`: calendar-year, never, or an MM-DD. `outside_spend`: a dated log ({date, amount, note}) of spend on the card the ledger never sees; a negative amount takes it back.
cards.name: Amazon Business Prime
